questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}$ for $x>0$, given $y=6$ when $x=2$.
Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2y$, given $y=2$ when $x=0$.
Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2x}{y^2}$, given $y=2$ when $x=0$.
Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y^2}{x}$ for $x>0$, given $y=1$ when $x=1$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y^2}=\dfrac{dx}{x}$. Integrate: $-\dfrac{1}{y}=\ln|x|+C$. Using $y=1,x=1$: $C=-1$. So $-\dfrac{1}{y}=\ln x-1$, giving $y=\dfrac{1}{1-\ln x}$.

sections.heading: First-order linear differential equations using an integrating factor

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+3y=12$ using an integrating factor, given $y=2$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{3x}$. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(ye^{3x})=12e^{3x}$. Integrate: $ye^{3x}=4e^{3x}+C$, so $y=4+Ce^{-3x}$. Using $y=2,x=0$: $C=-2$. Solution: $y=4-2e^{-3x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2y=e^{3x}$ using an integrating factor, given $y=1$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{-2x}$. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(ye^{-2x})=e^{3x}e^{-2x}=e^x$. Integrate: $ye^{-2x}=e^x+C$, so $y=e^{3x}+Ce^{2x}$. Using $y=1,x=0$: $C=0$. Solution: $y=e^{3x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=5$ using an integrating factor, given $y=0$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^x$. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(ye^x)=5e^x$. Integrate: $ye^x=5e^x+C$, so $y=5+Ce^{-x}$. Using $y=0,x=0$: $C=-5$. Solution: $y=5-5e^{-x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+4y=8$ using an integrating factor, given $y=3$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{4x}$. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(ye^{4x})=8e^{4x}$. Integrate: $ye^{4x}=2e^{4x}+C$, so $y=2+Ce^{-4x}$. Using $y=3,x=0$: $C=1$. Solution: $y=2+e^{-4x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{y}{x}=x^2$ for $x>0$ using an integrating factor, given $y=1$ when $x=1$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{\int\frac{1}{x}dx}=x$. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy)=x^3$. Integrate: $xy=\dfrac{x^4}{4}+C$, so $y=\dfrac{x^3}{4}+\dfrac{C}{x}$. Using $y=1,x=1$: $C=\dfrac{3}{4}$. Solution: $y=\dfrac{x^3}{4}+\dfrac{3}{4x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{2y}{x}=x^3$ for $x>0$ using an integrating factor, given $y=3$ when $x=1$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{\int-\frac{2}{x}dx}=x^{-2}$. $\dfrac{d}{dx}(yx^{-2})=x$. Integrate: $yx^{-2}=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+C$, so $y=\dfrac{x^4}{2}+Cx^2$. Using $y=3,x=1$: $C=\dfrac{5}{2}$. Solution: $y=\dfrac{x^4}{2}+\dfrac{5}{2}x^2$.

questions.q: Verify that $y=3e^{2x}$ satisfies $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2y=0$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=6e^{2x}$. Substituting: $6e^{2x}-2(3e^{2x})=6e^{2x}-6e^{2x}=0$, confirming the equation is satisfied.

questions.q: Verify that $y=x^2+Ce^{-x}$ is a general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=x^2+2x$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x-Ce^{-x}$. Substituting: $(2x-Ce^{-x})+(x^2+Ce^{-x})=2x+x^2$, which matches the right-hand side $x^2+2x$ exactly, confirming the equation is satisfied for any constant $C$.

questions.q: Verify that $y=\dfrac{1}{2}\sin(2x)$ satisfies $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+4y=0$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\cos(2x)$. $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-2\sin(2x)$. Substituting: $-2\sin(2x)+4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin(2x)\right)=-2\sin(2x)+2\sin(2x)=0$, confirming the equation is satisfied.

questions.q: Find the general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=4x^3-6x$, and explain what determines a particular solution from this family.
questions.answer: Integrating directly: $y=x^4-3x^2+C$. A particular solution is obtained by specifying one point that the curve must pass through, which fixes the value of the arbitrary constant $C$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a mixing tank

questions.q: This question has three parts. A tank contains $300$ litres of brine with $10$ kg of dissolved salt. Fresh water flows in at $6$ litres/minute, and the well-mixed solution flows out at the same rate, keeping the volume constant. Let $S(t)$ be the mass of salt (kg) at time $t$ minutes. (a) Explain why $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=-\dfrac{S}{50}$. (b) Solve this differential equation for $S(t)$, given $S(0)=10$. (c) Find how long it takes for the salt content to drop to $2$ kg, to the nearest minute.
questions.answer: (a) Since the incoming water carries no salt, salt only leaves, at a rate equal to concentration times outflow: $\dfrac{S}{300}\times6=\dfrac{S}{50}$ kg/min, so $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=-\dfrac{S}{50}$. (b) Separate: $\dfrac{dS}{S}=-\dfrac{dt}{50}$. Integrate: $\ln S=-\dfrac{t}{50}+C$, so $S=Ae^{-t/50}$. Using $S(0)=10$: $A=10$. Solution: $S(t)=10e^{-t/50}$. (c) $2=10e^{-t/50}\Rightarrow e^{-t/50}=0.2\Rightarrow-\dfrac{t}{50}=\ln0.2\approx-1.6094\Rightarrow t\approx80$ minutes.
